sourcedFrom: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) (2009)
cleanIntro: The WASR-10 is a Romanian-made stamped-receiver AK in 7.62x39 that Century imports and publishes the manual for, and Century's book is the document that ships with the rifle. Three things about this pattern shape the job. There is NO magazine disconnect: the rifle will fire with the magazine out if a round is in the chamber, which is why the magazine comes out first and the chamber is checked second, every time. The bolt carrier group comes out over the top with the receiver cover off, and the recoil spring guide is what retains that cover — so the cover and the spring are one sequence, not two. And the gas cylinder tube lifts off with the top handguard once its locking latch is rotated up, which is the only part of the gas system this book asks you to touch. Century says plainly that no further disassembly is generally needed for routine maintenance on this rifle.

steps.title: Safety lever fully UP to SAFE — listen for the click
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and rotate the big sheet-metal safety lever on the right side fully upward until you hear it click into place. In that position it physically blocks the trigger from moving. On an AK the lever is also what covers the charging handle slot, so full up is visible from a metre away and is worth confirming by eye as well as by ear.
steps.quote: 1. Place the safety lever in the “ON” or “SAFE” position by moving it to its fully upward position.You should hear an audible “click” when it is in place.This position prevents trigger movement. (See Illustration #2).
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Unloading Rifle — p.8

steps.title: Magazine out — press the release FORWARD
steps.action: The AK magazine catch is a lever in front of the trigger guard and it is pressed FORWARD, not sideways like an AR button. Press it forward while rocking the magazine's front lug out of the receiver and pull the magazine free. Lay it aside off the bench; it must be out of the rifle for the whole strip.
steps.quote: 2. Remove the magazine by pressing forward on the magazine release lever while pulling the magazine out of the rifle. (See Illustration #4).
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Unloading Rifle — p.8
steps.warn: WARNING! The rifle will fire if the magazine is removed and if the trigger is pulled when a cartridge is in the chamber.

steps.title: Operating handle fully back and LOOK into the chamber
steps.action: Draw the operating handle — the stub welded to the right of the bolt carrier — fully rearward and look down into the open action at the chamber. On this rifle you have to look; there is no hold-open on an empty chamber and nothing tells you the gun is clear except your own eyes. Keep the muzzle safe while you do it.
steps.caution: WARNING! Any firearm, if dropped, could fire if there is a cartridge in the chamber and the safety is in the fire position.
steps.quote: 3. Pull the operating handle back fully rearward and look into the open action to ensure there is no remaining cartridge in the barrel chamber. (See Illustration #5).
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Unloading Rifle — p.8

steps.title: Eye protection on before the receiver cover moves
steps.action: Put shooting glasses or goggles on. There is a compressed recoil spring under the receiver cover and it is the first thing the strip releases — Century names spring tension as the specific reason for the eye protection. Confirm one more time that the magazine is out and the chamber is empty before anything is pressed.
steps.quote: WARNING! Wear eye protection, such as shooting glasses or goggles when disassembling your firearm to protect your eyes from tensioned parts, such as springs, that could be dislodged during disassembly.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Rifle Disassembly — p.9
steps.warn: WARNING! Before beginning the disassembly process, check to ensure the rifle is unloaded. To do so, follow the procedures detailed previously in this manual.

steps.title: Receiver cover retainer button in, cover lifted off
steps.action: Find the retainer button at the top rear of the receiver — it is the protruding end of the recoil spring guide poking through the rear trunnion. Press it IN while you lift the rear of the top cover, and the cover comes free. Press without lifting and nothing happens; lift without pressing and you will bend the cover.
steps.prose: The recoil spring guide is the cover's latch, which is why this rifle's cover has no screws and comes off with one hand.
steps.quote: 2. Press in on the receiver cover retainer button located at the top rear of the rifle’s receiver while simultaneously lifting up on the rear of the receiver’s top cover and removing it. (See Illustration #6).
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Rifle Disassembly — p.9

steps.title: Recoil spring guide and spring forward out of their notch
steps.action: With the cover off, push the recoil spring guide FORWARD to lift its rear lug clear of the notch in the rear of the receiver, then let the spring extend and draw the whole assembly out. Keep a hand on it as it comes: it is a long spring under compression and it will jump if you let go at the wrong moment.
steps.quote: 3. Slide the recoil spring guide and spring forward, out of their notch in the rear of the receiver and remove.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Rifle Disassembly — p.9

steps.title: Bolt carrier group back and up out of the receiver
steps.action: The carrier is now free. Slide it rearward while lifting slightly on the operating handle, and when it reaches the end of the rails the whole assembly lifts out of the receiver to the rear. It only clears at the very back — if it will not come up, you have not run it far enough back.
steps.quote: 4. The bolt and carrier assembly is now free to move. Slide it to the rear while lifting upward slightly on the operating handle until the assembly can be lifted out of the receiver by pulling it to the rear.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Rifle Disassembly — p.9

steps.title: Bolt rotated out of the carrier
steps.action: Push the bolt to the rear of the carrier and rotate it so its lugs clear the raceway on the underside of the carrier, then pull it forward and out. Century describes the same separation twice on this page in slightly different words — the second wording says to turn it clockwise so the guiding lug comes out of the shaped recess in the bolt support. Either way it is a rotate-then-pull, never a straight yank.
steps.aside: 6. The bolt is removed from the carrier by pulling it rearward and then turning clockwise so that its guiding lug comes out of the shaped recess of the bolt support.Then pull bolt forward and out.
steps.quote: 5. The bolt is now removed by pushing it to the rear of the bolt carrier and then rotating it so that its lugs clear the raceway on the underside of the bolt carrier. It is then pulled forward and out of the carrier.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Rifle Disassembly — p.9

steps.title: Gas cylinder tube latch up, top handguard and tube off — strip complete
steps.action: Rotate the gas cylinder tube locking latch upward to free the tube, then lift the rear of the top handguard and take the handguard and tube off together. That is the WASR stripped: receiver cover, recoil spring assembly, bolt carrier, bolt, and the gas tube with its handguard. Century is explicit that no further disassembly is generally needed for routine maintenance on this rifle — do not chase the trigger group, the piston or the front sight block.
steps.quote: 7. Rotate the gas cylinder tube locking latch upward to free the gas cylinder tube. (See Illustration #7). Pull up on the rear of the top handguard to free and remove the tube.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Rifle Disassembly — p.9
steps.warn: No further disassembly is generally needed for routine maintenance. Clean the removed parts with a good quality gun cleaning solvent as well as the inside of the receiver.

steps.title: Bore: 7.62 brush wet with solvent, then patches to a clean patch
steps.action: Fit a correct-calibre brush to a rod, dampen it with solvent and push it through the barrel several times. Swap to a correctly sized patch and push that through several times to carry the loosened fouling out, then alternate brush and patches until a patch comes out clean. Work from the chamber end wherever the rifle lets you.
steps.quote:
3. To clean the barrel, select the correct caliber cleaning brush and attach it to a cleaning rod. 4. Dampen the brush with gun cleaning solvent and then push the brush through the barrel
several times. 5. Remove the brush and attach a correctly sized cloth cleaning patch to the cleaning rod and
push it through the barrel several times to remove loosened fouling. 6. Repeat this process with the brush and cleaning patches until a final patch comes out clean
after swabbing the bore.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — To Clean the Barrel — p.10

steps.title: Bolt, carrier, gas piston and the inside of the receiver
steps.action: Run the same brush-and-solvent process over the bolt and the other action parts: the bolt face and its lug recesses, the carrier rails, the gas piston head and the inside of the gas tube. A bronze or nylon bristle brush dabbed in solvent is the tool Century names. Wipe the inside of the receiver out while it is open — that is where the carbon collects on a piston gun.
steps.caution: WARNING! There may be sharp edges on parts of the firearm. Keep fingers protected, such as by wearing a pair of protective gloves when cleaning.
steps.quote: 7. Repeat the procedure just followed to clean the bolt and other action parts.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — To Clean the Barrel — p.10

steps.title: Outside surfaces: solvent, dry, then preservative oil
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the rifle down with a soft cloth dabbed in solvent to lift the residue, dry every surface you touched, and finish with a cloth dipped in a good preservative oil. Stamped AK receivers are thin and painted rather than deeply blued, so a wiped-and-oiled exterior is doing real work against rust here.
steps.quote:
8. Remove shooting residue from the rifle’s outside by wiping surfaces with a soft cloth dabbed in
solvent. Dry surfaces. 9. Finally, wipe down all outside surfaces with a soft cloth dipped in a good quality metal
preservative oil.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — To Clean the Barrel — p.10

steps.title: Light oil on carrier and bolt before it goes back together
steps.action: Before reassembly, oil the bolt carrier and the bolt LIGHTLY — the rails, the cam track and the bolt lugs. An AK runs wet-ish but not soaked; excess oil on a gas gun collects carbon into a paste. In freezing weather Century recommends a dry lubricant instead of oil.
steps.aside: Note: In freezing weather (below 32° F. or 0° C.), the use of a dry lubricant (instead of oil) for lubrication may work better.
steps.quote: Before reassembly, lightly oil the bolt carrier and bolt.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Rifle Disassembly — p.9

steps.title: Cleaning interval, and what to do before storage
steps.action: Clean as soon as possible after firing. Even unfired, Century wants this rifle cleaned once or twice a year in a dry climate and as often as weekly in a humid one. For storage, clean it thoroughly, lightly lubricate it, wipe the outside with good gun oil, and confirm it is unloaded and stored apart from its ammunition — and remove the excess oil and check the bore is dry before it is ever fired again.
steps.quote: Always clean your rifle as soon as possible after firing to prevent buildup of shooting residue and to prevent corrosion from starting.To maintain your rifle in good working order, it should be cleaned once or twice a year in low-humidity environments, even if it has not been fired. In a high humidity area, it may be necessary to clean your rifle as often as once a week.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — WASR TYPE SPORTING RIFLES — Cal. 7.62x39MM — 2009 ("© 2009 Century International Arms, Inc." printed on page 1) — Cleaning Intervals — p.10
steps.warn:
When rifle is to be reused, remove all excess lubrication before firing. Make sure
bore (inside of barrel) is dry and free of obstructions before firing.

deepAbsentReason: Century publishes nothing beyond this strip for the WASR. Its own sentence at the end of the disassembly sequence is that no further disassembly is generally needed for routine maintenance, and the remainder of the 12-page book is safety rules, loading, cleaning intervals and storage. There is no published trigger-group, gas-piston or front-end teardown to walk, and writing one would be inventing a deep clean for an imported rifle whose importer has deliberately not documented it.

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Correct-calibre brush on a rod, dampened with solvent, pushed through several times.
Correctly sized patches pushed through to carry the loosened fouling out.
Alternate brush and patches until a patch comes out clean.
Bore left dry and free of obstructions before the rifle is fired.

cleaning.name: Bolt and carrier
tasks: Bolt face and lug recesses brushed with solvent — this is where primer and case residue packs.
Carrier rails and cam track wiped clean.
Gas piston head and the inside of the gas cylinder tube brushed out.
Light oil on carrier and bolt before reassembly; dry lubricant instead below freezing.

cleaning.name: Receiver interior
tasks: Inside of the stamped receiver cleaned with solvent — a bronze or nylon bristle brush helps.
Rails and the rear trunnion notch wiped out.
Protective gloves: there are sharp edges on a stamped receiver.

cleaning.name: Exterior and storage
tasks: Outside surfaces wiped with a soft cloth dabbed in solvent, then dried.
All outside surfaces wiped with a good quality metal preservative oil.
Cleaning interval: after every firing; once or twice a year unfired in low humidity, up to weekly in high humidity.
For storage: thoroughly cleaned, lightly lubricated, unloaded, and kept separate from its ammunition.

reassembly: Gas cylinder tube: align its front opening with the gas cylinder, seat the rear into the rear sight base, and rotate the gas cylinder tube lock DOWN to lock it.
Bolt into the carrier: enter it from the front to the rear, then rotate the bolt to the LEFT so it can be pushed to the front of the carrier.

Holding the carrier so the bolt stays with it, enter the assembly into the receiver, pushing the gas piston end into its protection tube and pressing the carrier's guide ribs into the corresponding grooves at the rear of the receiver; then push the carrier forward.

Recoil spring assembly pushed into the boring in the bolt carrier; the rear end of the guide enters the groove in the rear of the receiver by pressing the spring forward and downward, then letting the guide move gently rearward.

Receiver cover: front end into the groove at the rear end of the piston protection tube, then press the cover down so the catch on the end of the recoil spring guide enters the cutout in the rear of the cover.
Safety lever back up to SAFE.
fncheck: With the rifle proven empty, the magazine out and the muzzle in a safe direction: press down on the receiver cover and confirm the recoil spring guide's catch is holding it — a cover that lifts is a cover that will leave the rifle when it is fired. Cycle the operating handle through several full strokes and confirm the carrier runs to the rear stop and returns fully forward under spring pressure with no hesitation. Rotate the safety fully up and confirm the trigger will not move, then down and confirm it will. Check the gas tube latch is fully rotated down and the handguard is captive. Finally, confirm the bore is dry, free of obstructions and free of excess oil before any ammunition is near the rifle.
